text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure usually has no warning signs or symptoms, which is why it is often called the "silent killer".

list.snippet: No physical clues: Most people with high blood pressure feel completely normal and do not know they have it.
Regular checks needed: You must get your blood pressure measured by a healthcare provider or home monitor to know your status.
Hidden damage: Untreated high blood pressure can still damage your heart, brain, kidneys, and eyes over time without you feeling sick.

text_blocks.snippet: If your blood pressure becomes extremely high or rises rapidly, you might notice subtle or severe signs:

list.snippet: Headaches: Early-morning dull headaches, especially at the back of the head.
Vision changes: Blurred vision or eye strain.
Dizziness: Feeling lightheaded, woozy, or unsteady.
Fatigue: Feeling unusually exhausted because your heart works harder to pump blood.
Pounding: A rhythmic thumping sensation in your ears, neck, or chest.

text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure above 180/120 mm Hg is a dangerous crisis that requires emergency medical care (call 911). Watch for:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Sudden weakness, numbness, or facial drooping (signs of stroke)

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about prevention and care through the CDC About High Blood Pressure or get official medical guidance from the Mayo Clinic High Blood Pressure Overview.

list.snippet: What was your recent blood pressure reading?
